item.title: Reading a store
item.description:
Every view here is computed when you ask, so none of them can be stale.

What should I do?

tik next --actor alice
tik next --role :triager
tik explain 3184 --actor alice

next ranks by how much downstream work each step unlocks, with quiet tickets rising. A step that would replace a fact already settled, such as offering :declined on a request whose decision is :accepted, is marked (overrides a settled fact), names the value it replaces on each ticket, and ranks after every step that only adds evidence:

item.title: Recording work
item.description:
You record evidence. Stages follow.

Create a ticket

tik new support-request --title "login fails on Firefox"

The ticket pins the process definition’s content hash at creation, so it is judged by the rules it was minted under until somebody deliberately moves it with tik reprocess.

Created beneath a store, a ticket inherits its context as signed facts: repo=<name> from the enclosing git repository, plus any .tik-facts.edn maps on the way down, nearest winning, with anything explicit beating both.

item.title: Store administration
item.description:
Identity

tik actor add alice ~/.config/tik/id_ed25519.pub
tik sign 3184
tik witness 3184

actor add registers a signer in the store’s allowed-signers registry. An actor name is letters, digits and ._@+-, and the key file holds one OpenSSH public key on one line; anything else is refused, because the name and key are written verbatim into the registry, where *, ?, ! and , are principal patterns and a line break starts another grant. A rung-2 binding (tik bridge oidc, tik bridge workload) whose actor or key fails the same check grants nothing.
